So the unreported median imputer (Colab.py:515-527) touches 33x39 cells and nothing else, and the 'different record set' point is 33 specific rows plus the 12 collapsed duplicate sleep rows — not an unknown fraction.

Exposure scope of the identifier finding is smaller than reported: outputs_paper_exact/ is gitignored (.gitignore:75) and *.ipynb is gitignored (.gitignore:39), so `git ls-files` tracks only Training/XAI_Paper_Reproduction2_PaperExact_Colab.py and the three .md files. The 174 e-mail-shaped ids exist in the working tree and on the Colab Drive, not in repository history — the reader's phrase 'written into repository output CSVs' overstates it, and the .ipynb the reader lists as an entry file is not version-controlled at all.

sleep_period_id is kept as a model feature (feature_columns.json:60; rank 58, mean |SHAP| 0.1519 at shap_importance_full.csv:59) even though the pipeline collapses every (patient_id, wake-date) to a single sleep period (Colab.py:404-408). PAPER_PROTOCOL.md:74 cites sleep_period_id's presence in Figure 2 as the reason to believe the paper did NOT de-duplicate, so this implementation keeps a column whose meaning its own preprocessing has destroyed — a sharper version of deviation 2 that the reader did not connect.

Two mutually inconsistent SHAP rankings coexist and neither is ever scored against Figure 6. The OOF ranking over all 86 features (Colab.py:695-703 -> shap_importance_full.csv) drives feature selection; a separate full-fit ranking over the 40 selected features (Colab.py:889-900 -> final/shap_importance_positive.csv) drives the SHAP summary plot and the `top_features` block written into dementia_risk_score_summary.json (Colab.py:946). They disagree materially — activity_class_5min_count_2 is rank 29 in the OOF ranking and rank 5 in the full-fit one, sleep_rmssd 5 vs 4 — and RESULTS_REVIEW_KO.md:233-236 compares the paper's Figure 6 against only 2 of its 20 features, so no Figure-6 rank agreement is measured anywhere. The reader's 'top-3 SHAP features match Figure 6' used only the OOF file.

No class-imbalance handling anywhere despite the paper's 1.74:1 record ratio (7,737 vs 4,446): no class_weight, scale_pos_weight or is_unbalance in any of the seven estimators or in the final LightGBM (Colab.py:531-545), and a hard 0.5 threshold at every stage (Colab.py:587, 817, 884). This matters because accuracy/precision/recall/F1 comparisons with Table 1 all hinge on a threshold PAPER_PROTOCOL.md:163 marks NOT REPORTED — positive-class recall is 0.6658 for the baseline LightGBM (baselines/model_comparison.csv:2) and 0.7791 for the final model (final_cv_metrics.json:59), i.e. the models miss a quarter to a third of impaired days at that threshold while the macro numbers still look close to the paper.

The audit's DRS range tolerance is near-vacuous and the reader mentioned the tolerances without testing them: DRS_RANGE_TOLERANCE = 3.50 (Colab.py:187) passes an impaired max of 32.4858 against the paper's 31.28 (delta +1.21) and a CN min of 0.5225 against 1.06 (delta -0.54), on a score whose whole observed spread is roughly 0.5-32.5. Combined with the count-only feature checks (Colab.py:1065-1066) and the +/-0.01 AUC bands, `paper_exact_audit.json`'s single FAIL is structurally incapable of surfacing the feature-set mismatch, so 'audit passed except best_k' understates the gap.

Seed handling is inconsistent across stages and there is no seed sensitivity at all: RANDOM_STATE=42 serves simultaneously as the fold-split seed and the model seed (Colab.py:547-550, 711, 814), but the SHAP-ranking model alone varies per fold via `random_state=random_state + fold` (Colab.py:690). One seed, no repeats, no SD/CI/bootstrap anywhere in the code — so every headline number (0.8995 / 0.9026 / 0.9479) is a single draw, and the k=39-vs-40 FAIL that the review treats as the one substantive gap is a single-draw result whose stability was never tested (the only seed-variation code, Colab.py:777-798, is disabled and outcome-driven).

The DRS t-tests take the CN mean as a known population constant when it is estimated from the same rows (Colab.py:917-919 daily; :920-923 subject-level), which compounds the subject-clustering problem the reader raised: both p-values (0.0 and 3.44e-29, RESULTS_REVIEW_KO.md:394,404) are therefore uninterpretable as evidence, and audit checks drs_impaired_mean_gt_cn and drs_p_lt_0_05 (Colab.py:1073-1074) are guaranteed to pass whenever the group means differ at all.
